questions.q: What's the difference between a data source and a dataset?
options: A data source is the connection (server, database, credentials); a dataset is a query run against that connection, producing rows and columns
They're two names for exactly the same object
A dataset is the connection; a data source is the query
A data source only works with Excel files, a dataset only works with SQL Server
questions.explain: A data source and dataset are always a pair: the data source is the connection, and the dataset is a query run against it that actually produces the fields you drag onto the design surface.

questions.q: What's the practical benefit of a shared data source over an embedded one?
options: Change the connection once on the report server, and every report referencing that shared data source picks up the change automatically
Shared data sources run queries faster than embedded ones
Embedded data sources cannot connect to SQL Server
Shared data sources don't require a connection string
questions.explain: An embedded data source is saved inside one report only, so five reports using the same connection means five copies to maintain. A shared data source is published once and referenced by many reports.

questions.q: Where do you add a new data source or dataset in Report Builder?
options: From the Report Data pane's New menu
From the Insert tab's ribbon only
By right-clicking the design surface body
Datasets can only be added through SQL Server Management Studio
questions.explain: On the Report Data pane's menu, select New, then Data Source (or right-click an existing data source and select Add Dataset).

questions.q: In the Dataset Properties dialog's Query page, what does the Text query type let you do?
options: Write a query directly using the query language of the data source, such as a T-SQL SELECT statement
Automatically return every field in every table in the database
Only run stored procedures, never raw SQL
Connect exclusively to shared datasets on the report server
questions.explain: Text is one of three query type options (alongside Table and StoredProcedure) and is what you'll use for most real reports — writing an actual SQL query.

questions.q: What happens when you click Refresh Fields (or OK) after writing a dataset's query?
options: The query runs once against the data source, and the resulting field collection appears under the dataset node in the Report Data pane
The report immediately publishes to the report server
The data source is permanently converted from embedded to shared
Nothing — fields must be typed in manually
questions.explain: Running the query populates the dataset's field collection — the list of columns available to drag onto data regions on the design surface.
